bug_semantics: When user tracking is enabled (installer default main.enableUserTracking=true), frontend visits append the raw QUERY_STRING and Referer to content/core/data/trackingDDMMYYYY under the web root. Default Apache rules only denied ZIP files under content/, so the tracking file was unauthenticated-readable. Commit 41d7436f5bb7d4b7954a74d1c8f1f36bd157ffcf replaced plaintext emailed passwords with a signed reset URL of the form /index.php?action=resetpw&u=<id>&exp=<ts>&sig=<hmac> and added phpmyfaq/resetpw.php, which calls userTracking('reset_password') on GET without consuming the token. Opening the emailed link therefore wrote u/exp/sig into the public tracking file; an attacker could replay those parameters against POST /api/user/password/reset until expiry or password change.
flaw_origin: Pre-existing public tracking already wrote QUERY_STRING to content/core/data/trackingDDMMYYYY. The account-takeover secret first appeared when 41d7436f5bb7d4b7954a74d1c8f1f36bd157ffcf put a reusable HMAC reset token in that query string and tracked the reset-page GET. Parent e3927a31b23ed142b92e195512dd8e04675010de still emailed a generated password and has no action=resetpw, signResetToken, or resetpw.php. The 4.1.7 closer is b1d405e267964f822b6bf228ef69e77f84c4240e (redact query/referer; deny content/core/data).
ai_marker: none on BIC commit object: author and committer Thorsten Rinne <thorsten@phpmyfaq.de>; GitHub login thorsten; message only 'fix: replace plaintext password reset with signed token flow'; no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot author.
evidence: Vendor GHSA-j5w2-cwwj-xj7x (patched 4.1.7) and CVE-2026-75918 (CVE.org state PUBLISHED, VulnCheck CNA; GHSA-hccc-74hg-j43v withdrawn_at null) describe public trackingDDMMYYYY leaking reset tokens. git log -S action=resetpw and -S signResetToken first hit 41d7436f5bb7d4b7954a74d1c8f1f36bd157ffcf (single parent e3927a31b23ed142b92e195512dd8e04675010de). git cat-file -p 41d7436f5bb7d4b7954a74d1c8f1f36bd157ffcf: author/committer Thorsten Rinne <thorsten@phpmyfaq.de>, no AI trailers. git cat-file -e parent:phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Controller/Frontend/UnauthorizedUserController.php succeeds; parent:phpmyfaq/resetpw.php fails. Parent tree lacks action=resetpw/signResetToken; BIC tree has sprintf reset URL and resetpw.php userTracking(reset_password). Parent already writes QUERY_STRING to PMF_ROOT_DIR/content/core/data/tracking{dmY} and .htaccess only F-blocks content/*.zip. 4.1.6 contains both the reset URL and unredacted tracking; 4.1.6..4.1.7 on those paths is b1d405e267964f822b6bf228ef69e77f84c4240e (Utils::redactSensitiveQueryString/Url plus RewriteRule ^content/core/data). Later 9d2bfc0ef95b7ce4494d8ea098ea6c22ea5d8564 is not an ancestor of 4.1.7.
reasoning: The advisory is a real CWE-200 leak of live password-reset HMAC material from a world-readable tracking log, not a withdrawn/rejected CVE. The smallest commit that first wrote the secret-bearing lines is 41d7436f5bb7d4b7954a74d1c8f1f36bd157ffcf: it introduced the query-string reset token and the reset-page GET that logs it. Tracking of raw QUERY_STRING into a public file predates that commit and is not the BIC for this token-replay bug; parent still mailed a one-shot plaintext password. That BIC is a single-parent non-squash first-write by human maintainer Thorsten Rinne with no AI markers on the commit object, so authorship is NOT_AI. The 4.1.7 patch that closes the leak is b1d405e267964f822b6bf228ef69e77f84c4240e.
